title: Ethical Leadership and Human Drivers of Industry 4.0 Readiness in Manufacturing SMEs: A Configurational Analysis
content: Manufacturing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) face significant challenges in implementing Industry 4.0 because digital transformation requires not only technological capabilities but also appropriate human, ethical and organizational conditions. This study examines configurations of ethical leadership, leader integrity, work engagement and employee creativity that are sufficient for high Industry 4.0 readiness. Using fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), survey data from 156 employees and managers representing 58 automotive manufacturing SMEs in Poland were aggregated to the enterprise level and analyzed configurationally. The results identify three alternative configurations sufficient for high Industry 4.0 readiness and two configurations sufficient for low readiness. No single analyzed condition was necessary for either high or low readiness, indicating that Industry 4.0 readiness is associated with different combinations of leadership- and employ-ee-related conditions. Ethical leadership and work engagement recur as prominent conditions in the high-readiness solution structure, while their absence appears in configurations associated with low readiness. The findings highlight the importance of human and ethical conditions for Industry 4.0 readiness and extend the configurational perspective on digital transformation by identifying alternative combinations of leadership- and employee-related factors. These insights are also relevant to discussions of sustainable digital transformation and the human-centric orientation of Industry 5.0.
